title: Primary Care, Weather, and the Missed Opportunity for Savings
abstract: Extreme weather is a recurring source of stress on healthcare delivery, yet health systems remain largely reactive. Unlike an individual medical emergency, which the system absorbs one case at a time, a heat wave, wildfire smoke episode, or storm affects an entire population simultaneously. The resulting surge degrades care for every emergency patient, not only those the weather directly harmed. Primary care that anticipates weather-related risk and intervenes proactively can blunt that surge, but a central barrier to scaling such care is economic rather than clinical. Conventional prevention accounting counts only the benefit to the treated patient, and fee-for-service payment offers primary care practices only limited and poorly matched means to fund anticipatory care. Payment models that reward keeping patients healthy, such as global budgets, can address this, but only if risk adjustment accounts for environmental exposure so that providers serving vulnerable populations are not penalized. To address this, we outline 4 priorities: evaluations that capture system-wide costs; payment that rewards anticipatory care and adjusts for environmental risk; supply-side resilience in primary care, built jointly with public health agencies; and data infrastructure linking exposure to healthcare utilization.
abstract_zh: 极端天气是医疗服务提供持续承受压力的一个反复出现的来源，然而卫生系统在很大程度上仍然是被动应对的。与卫生系统逐例吸收的个体医疗急症不同，热浪、野火烟雾事件或风暴会同时影响整个人群。由此产生的就诊高峰会降低所有急诊患者的救治质量，而不仅仅是那些直接受天气伤害的患者。能够预见天气相关风险并主动干预的初级保健，可以削弱这一就诊高峰，但推广此类医疗服务的核心障碍在于经济层面而非临床层面。传统的预防核算只计入受治疗患者的收益，而按服务收费的支付方式只为初级保健机构提供了有限且匹配不佳的资金来源以支持预防性医疗。能够奖励保持患者健康的支付模式（如整体预算制）可以解决这一问题，但前提是风险调整必须考虑环境暴露，以免对服务于弱势人群的医疗机构造成不利影响。为此，我们提出4项优先事项：能够反映全系统成本的评估；奖励预防性医疗并对环境风险进行调整的支付方式；与公共卫生机构共同建设的初级保健供给侧韧性；以及将暴露与医疗利用联系起来的数据基础设施。

Drought-Induced Deforestation in the Brazilian Amazon
abstract: This paper examines drought-induced deforestation in the Brazilian Legal Amazon and investigates the economics behind it. We focus on agricultural drought to study differential roles of family versus commercial farms in this region. Using high-resolution root-zone soil moisture and land cover data, we document that increases in soil moisture deficits lead to higher deforestation within the same year, with no detectable within-year feedback from local deforestation to local rainfall once we condition on prior forest stock. Our heterogeneity analyses by family-farm area shares across 770 municipalities reveal the critical role of resource-restricted family farms: (1) drought only raises deforestation where family farming predominates, and not where commercial agriculture dominates; (2) forest-related environmental fines rise rather than fall in high-family-farm municipalities during droughts, ruling out weaker monitoring; (3) high-family-farm municipalities see staple output fall, credit contract, and irrigation fail to expand, while low-family-farm municipalities suffer large cattle losses. Our estimates show that agricultural drought accounts for roughly 331 square kilometers of primary forest clearing during 2006-2019, committing carbon damages of about $135 million per year.
abstract_zh: 本文考察了巴西法定亚马逊地区由干旱引发的森林砍伐，并探讨了其背后的经济学机制。我们关注农业干旱，以研究家庭农场与商业农场在该地区所扮演的不同角色。利用高分辨率根区土壤水分和土地覆盖数据，我们发现土壤水分亏缺增加会导致同一年内森林砍伐增加；在控制了先前的森林存量后，并未发现局部森林砍伐对局部降雨产生可检测的年内反馈。我们按照770个市镇中家庭农场面积占比进行的异质性分析，揭示了资源受限的家庭农场所起的关键作用：（1）干旱只在家庭农业占主导的地区提高了森林砍伐，而在商业农业占主导的地区则没有；（2）在家庭农场比例较高的市镇，干旱期间与森林相关的环境罚款不降反升，这排除了监测力度减弱的解释；（3）家庭农场比例较高的市镇，主要粮食产出下降，信贷合同萎缩，灌溉也未能扩大，而家庭农场比例较低的市镇则遭受了大规模的牲畜损失。我们的估计表明，在2006–2019年间，农业干旱约导致33,100平方公里原始森林被砍伐，每年造成约1.35亿美元的碳损害。

Beyond the Canopy: How Satellite Data Detection Thresholds Influence Policy Evaluation and Deforestation Behavior
venue: Journal of Environmental Economics and Management
abstract: Satellite data is essential for enforcing and evaluating environmental policy, but technological limitations of monitoring systems can create perverse incentives and bias impact assessment. This study examines how detection thresholds in satellite monitoring systems affect both the implementation and evaluation of forest conservation policies. We identify three key mechanisms: a measurement issue, where datasets with larger minimum detection thresholds systematically miss small-scale deforestation; a loophole effect, where policy only reduces detectable, large-scale deforestation; and strategic adaptation, where regulated agents adjust behavior to exploit known detection thresholds, substituting from large- to small-scale deforestation. Studying Brazil’s 2008 municipal Blacklisting policy, we find that the government’s primary monitoring system, which does not report patches below 6.25 hectares, overestimates policy effectiveness by a third compared to datasets with smaller minimum detection thresholds. When measured with those datasets, blacklisting reduced deforestation by 31.2 % from baseline—substantially less than the 47.6 % reduction suggested by government data. Average clearing size declined by 28.9 %, with significant increases in patches below detection thresholds, reflecting both undetected and strategically fragmented activity. Our analysis reveals a critical challenge for environmental governance: as monitoring systems improve, so too do evasion strategies, requiring close attention to how technology shapes observed outcomes and on-the-ground incentives.
abstract_zh: 卫星数据对于执行和评估环境政策至关重要，但监测系统的技术局限可能产生扭曲的激励，并使影响评估产生偏差。本研究考察了卫星监测系统中的探测阈值如何影响森林保护政策的执行和评估。我们识别出三种关键机制：测量问题，即最小探测阈值较大的数据集会系统性地遗漏小规模的森林砍伐；漏洞效应，即政策仅减少了可探测到的大规模森林砍伐；以及策略性适应，即受监管主体调整行为，以利用已知的探测阈值，从大规模砍伐转向小规模砍伐。以巴西2008年的市级“黑名单”政策为研究对象，我们发现，政府的主要监测系统不报告低于6.25公顷的图斑，与最小探测阈值更小的数据集相比，它将政策效果高估了三分之一。使用那些数据集进行测量时，黑名单政策使森林砍伐相对于基线降低了31.2%，远低于政府数据所显示的47.6%的降幅。平均砍伐面积下降了28.9%，同时低于探测阈值的图斑显著增加，这既反映了未被发现的活动，也反映了策略性的碎片化行为。我们的分析揭示了环境治理面临的一项关键挑战：随着监测系统的改进，规避策略也随之升级，因此需要密切关注技术如何塑造观测到的结果以及实地激励。

Collective Property Rights Lead to Secondary Forest Growth in the Brazilian Amazon
venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
abstract: Forests serve a crucial role in our fight against climate change. Secondary forests provide important potential for conservation of biodiversity and climate change mitigation. In this paper, we explore whether collective property rights in the form of indigenous territories (ITs) lead to higher rates of secondary forest growth in previously deforested areas. We exploit the timing of granting of property rights, the geographic boundaries of ITs and two different methods, regression discontinuity design and difference-in-difference, to recover causal estimates. We find strong evidence that indigenous territories with secure tenure not only reduce deforestation inside their lands but also lead to higher secondary forest growth on previously deforested areas. After receiving full property rights, land inside ITs displayed higher secondary forest growth than land outside ITs, with an estimated effect of 5% using our main RDD specification, and 2.21% using our difference-in-difference research design. Furthermore, we estimate that the average age of secondary forests was 2.2 y older inside ITs with secure tenure using our main RDD specification, and 2.8 y older when using our difference-in-difference research design. Together, these findings provide evidence for the role that collective property rights can play in the push to restore forest ecosystems.
abstract_zh: 森林在我们应对气候变化的斗争中发挥着至关重要的作用。次生林为生物多样性保护和气候变化减缓提供了重要的潜力。在本文中，我们探讨了以原住民领地（ITs）形式存在的集体产权，是否会促使先前被砍伐的地区次生林的生长速度更快。我们利用产权授予的时间、原住民领地的地理边界，以及断点回归设计和双重差分两种方法，以获得因果估计。我们发现有力证据表明，拥有稳定土地使用权的原住民领地不仅减少了其领地内的森林砍伐，还促进了先前被砍伐地区次生林的更快生长。在获得完整产权之后，原住民领地内的土地表现出比领地外土地更快的次生林生长，在我们的主要断点回归设定下，估计效应为5%，而在双重差分研究设计下则为2.21%。此外，我们估计，在我们的主要断点回归设定下，拥有稳定土地使用权的原住民领地内次生林的平均林龄要高2.2年，而在双重差分研究设计下则高2.8年。总之，这些发现为集体产权在推动森林生态系统恢复方面可能发挥的作用提供了证据。

title: Incentives for Rural Households to Establish Tree Cover on Agricultural Land in Andhra Pradesh, India
venue: Environmental Economics in Developing Countries: Issues and Challenges
abstract: We explore the incentives of farmers to establish forest cover on agricultural land in Andhra Pradesh, India. A large body of theoretical economic work on land-use decisions examines the opportunity costs of switching land uses from agriculture to forest production (Parks and Hardie 1995; Haim 2011; Amacher et al. 2009), but empirical work that estimates the drivers of margin changes for these problems is still needed (Park et al. 1998). Based on a large dataset collected using a randomized survey of farm households in the East and West Godhavari regions in Andhra Pradesh, we use a multilevel mixed-effects probit model to analyze the decision to plant trees on private lands. We find that the most important positive drivers in the decision to plant trees are total land area, years of land tenure, and off-farm labour opportunity. However, factors that lower tree planting incentives are irrigation availability, average travel time to managed plots, elevation, and belonging to the scheduled tribes’ social group. Moreover, we find evidence that the probability of tree planting is not only associated with important fixed effects (the same across all households in our sample), but it is also associated with random effects that vary from village to village and with the number of plots that the household manages.
abstract_zh: 我们考察了印度安得拉邦农户在农业用地上建立森林覆盖的激励因素。关于土地利用决策的大量理论经济学研究探讨了将土地从农业转为林业生产的机会成本（Parks and Hardie 1995；Haim 2011；Amacher et al. 2009），但对于驱动这些边际变化的因素，仍需要实证研究（Park et al. 1998）。基于在安得拉邦东、西戈达瓦里地区对农户进行随机抽样调查所收集的大规模数据集，我们使用多层混合效应概率模型，分析农户在私有土地上种植树木的决策。我们发现，促进种树决策的最重要的正向因素是土地总面积、土地使用权年限以及非农劳动机会。然而，降低种树激励的因素包括灌溉可得性、到管理地块的平均路程时间、海拔，以及属于表列部落（Scheduled Tribes）社会群体。此外，我们发现，种树概率不仅与重要的固定效应（在我们的样本中所有家庭相同）相关，还与因村庄而异的随机效应以及该家庭所管理的地块数量相关。
